chain.title: One Big Compartment
chain.desc: Oak planks ringing a wooden chest; the Oak Drawer (1x1) holds a single item type but thirty-two stacks of it.

chain.title: Cut in Half
chain.desc: The same planks-and-chest recipe in the 1x2 arrangement, giving two independent compartments in one block.

chain.title: Four to a Face
chain.desc: The 2x2 arrangement, the densest plain drawer and the one most walls are built from.

chain.title: A Drawer That Holds Liquid
chain.desc: A bucket surrounded by planks; the Fluid Drawer stores fluids the way the wooden ones store items.

chain.title: Ready to Be Disguised
chain.desc: A wooden chest and iron nuggets make the Framed Drawer, which takes on the texture of any block you apply to it.

chain.title: The Upgrade That Isn't
chain.desc: Iron ingots on a drawer make the Iron Downgrade, which CUTS each slot back to a maximum of 64 items instead of raising it.

chain.title: Capacity, First Rung
chain.desc: A copper block, copper ingots, a wooden chest and a drawer; the bottom of the real capacity ladder, which starts at copper and not iron.

chain.title: Ingots and Blocks Together
chain.desc: Iron, stone, a piston and a drawer; it pools an item and its compressed block form as one quantity.

chain.title: All Three Sizes
chain.desc: The fuller version of the same recipe, handling nugget, ingot and block in one block instead of two tiers.

chain.title: Overflow Goes Nowhere
chain.desc: Obsidian applied to a drawer; once the compartment is full, anything more that goes in is deleted rather than rejected.

chain.title: Taking It Out
chain.desc: A hopper, redstone and stone worked onto a drawer; slotted in, it pulls items out of the drawer into whatever it faces.

chain.title: Putting It In
chain.desc: The mirror of the puller, built from the same hopper and redstone frame, feeding the drawer from an adjacent inventory.

chain.title: Sweeping the Ground
chain.desc: The third of the hopper-frame upgrades; it vacuums loose item entities off the floor in front of the drawer.

chain.title: Reading the Fill Level
chain.desc: A comparator, redstone and a redstone block on a drawer, so the block emits a signal that tracks how full it is.

chain.title: Capacity, Second Rung
chain.desc: Gold ingots and a gold block worked into the copper upgrade; each rung of this ladder is built from the one below it.

chain.title: One Address for the Wall
chain.desc: A quartz block, a comparator, stone and a drawer; every drawer it can reach becomes a single inventory.

chain.title: A Second Doorway
chain.desc: A quartz block, a repeater, stone and a drawer make the Controller Access Point, giving pipes another way onto the same network.

chain.title: Wiring by Hand
chain.desc: Gold, a diamond, paper and a drawer; it binds drawers to a controller that they do not physically touch.

chain.title: Setting the Rules
chain.desc: Gold, an emerald, paper and a drawer; it toggles per-drawer settings like locking, voiding and rendering.

chain.title: The Same Drawer Everywhere
chain.desc: An ender chest, planks and a drawer; drawers sharing a frequency share their contents across any distance.

chain.title: Capacity, Third Rung
chain.desc: Diamonds and a diamond block worked into the gold upgrade.

chain.title: A Wall for the Gear
chain.desc: Netherite, stone, a comparator and a drawer; unlike every other block here it takes tools and armour rather than one stacking item.

chain.title: Capacity, Last Rung
chain.desc: Made in a smithing table from the diamond upgrade, a netherite upgrade template and a netherite ingot.

notes:
60 ids verified: 60 assets/functionalstorage/models/item/*.json stems, all 60 carrying a block.functionalstorage.X or item.functionalstorage.X lang key, with 46 of them additionally confirmed by a blockstate AND a block loot table. The naive intersection rule finds 60 of 60 here - this mod names everything plainly, and unlike Storage Drawers it does NOT compose wood names, it writes them out one per key (block.functionalstorage.acacia_4 = 'Acacia Drawer (2x2)').

RECIPE-PARSING TRAP - 60 of the 69 recipe files are type forge:conditional, which means the real recipe (type, ingredients and result) is nested at recipes[0].recipe. A parser that reads the top-level 'result' finds NOTHING for 60 of 69 files and concludes the mod has almost no craftable content. The conditions themselves are trivial (forge:item_exists on the recipe's own output), so every one of them actually loads. Results below are read from the unwrapped inner recipe.

UPGRADE LADDER - counter-intuitive in the same way Storage Drawers is, and worth gating on. The tier enum in com/buuz135/functionalstorage/item/StorageUpgradeItem$StorageTier.class is COPPER, GOLD, DIAMOND, NETHERITE, IRON, MAX_STORAGE. IRON IS NOT ON THE LADDER: it is registered as functionalstorage:iron_downgrade, and the lang line item.utility.downgrade says 'Downgrades the slots to a max of 64 items'. Anyone assuming iron sits between copper and gold has it exactly backwards. The real capacity chain is copper -> gold -> diamond -> netherite, and each rung is crafted FROM the rung below (netherite via smithing_transform), so the order is a hard recipe dependency, not a guess.

DROPPED - functionalstorage:max_storage_upgrade and functionalstorage:creative_vending_upgrade. Both are genuinely registered (item model, item.functionalstorage.X lang key, and MAX_STORAGE is a StorageTier enum constant) but NEITHER has a recipe file, a loot table or a trade anywhere in the jar. moddb lists max_storage_upgrade at pos 1.000 in 3 packs, which is a good example of consensus recording something a pack added itself rather than something the mod ships. Questing either one from the base mod is uncompletable.

CONSENSUS CONFLICT, recipe graph preferred: moddb puts functionalstorage:storage_controller at pos 0.000, tied for first with oak_1. The controller recipe requires the functionalstorage:drawer item tag in two slots, and that tag lists only the 33 drawer blocks - a drawer has to exist before a controller can be crafted. It also costs a quartz block and a comparator against the drawer's chest and planks. The controller is placed at step 16 here. This is the same failure moddb made with storagedrawers, where it put controller before upgrade_template.
SECOND CONFLICT: moddb orders copper_upgrade (0.295) -> gold_upgrade (0.424) -> diamond_upgrade (0.735) -> netherite_upgrade (0.955) correctly, but never mentions iron_downgrade at all, so a generator following consensus alone would silently present iron as absent rather than as a deliberate downgrade.

WOOD VARIANTS ARE A WHEEL, NOT CHAIN STEPS. Ten woods (oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark_oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped) times three sizes is 30 blocks that are one idea in thirty planks; there is no bamboo drawer. The mod itself treats them as interchangeable - data/functionalstorage/recipes/oak_drawer_alternate_x*.json uses a custom ingredient of type functionalstorage:woodless which accepts any plank not matched by a dedicated recipe and still outputs oak_1, so modded woods work without new blocks. The framed family (6 blocks) is a second such wheel.

SCOPE NOTE - the seven data/functionalstorage/recipes/custom_compacting/*.json files (amethyst, clay, glowstone, ice, melon, packed_ice, quartz) are not items. They declare which non-ingot materials the compacting drawers know how to compress, and are why the compacting drawer is worth a chain slot at all.
